TcpStack: StartFin signals the window after it closes the write side, as Close and Dispose do, so a writer parked on the window wakes without the stream's cancellation (Fable's finding)

TcpStack: a new connection is wired (Start: the stack reference, the stream, the maintenance interest) before the table publishes it to the sweeps, DropAllConnections and the receive path, where it was published first - safe only with the serial receive loop and an unguessable ISN (Fable's finding)

TcpStack: the zero-window probe goes out only on a zero window (RFC 9293 3.8.6.1); a full but open window waits for its ACK like a full ring, the RTO covering its loss, where a late ACK drew a probe byte past the window's right edge; a test checks that no byte goes past it (Fable's finding)

TcpStack: the connection table's key is ConnectionKey - the segment's addresses read as numbers from the packet, its ports and its IP version - where an endpoint pair needed an IPAddress per segment: a segment of a known connection allocates nothing in the stack (one 40-byte IPAddress before, on parsed IPv4 packets), and the stack's work per pure-ACK segment fell from about 230 to 100 ns; the SYN and the RST of an unknown flow build their endpoint pair as before; a test keeps an IPv6 flow apart from an IPv4 one with the same numbers (a third-party review's finding)

TcpStack: the orphan's idle clock starts at the close, where it started at the idle sweep after it - until that sweep the peer's no-progress ACKs kept the orphan from eviction, and its idle timeout fired up to one IdleCheckInterval late; a test evicts an orphan before the first sweep (a third-party review's finding)

TcpStack: the SYN-ACK carries our Window Scale option only when the SYN carried one (RFC 7323 2.2), where it always did; the parser tells an absent option from a shift of 0, and a test checks the SYN-ACK of each (a third-party review's finding)
